organizations.csv: Key quality, for the engineer at validation (not a mapping question): acct_num is blank on 13 rows and has 18 duplicate values, while organization.organization_id is required and must be unique per entity. Duplicate ids re-sent with different content produce a 409 conflict under the target cross-record rules, so the duplicates must be resolved or the rows merged before load, and the 13 keyless rows cannot be loaded at all (they also strand their primary_contact_email, since contact.organization_id must reference an existing organization).

company_name shows 45 normalized duplicates and 11 case-variant groups against 996 distinct values. Combined with the 18 duplicate acct_num values, this suggests the file contains the same company more than once. Worth a dedupe pass before load.

Future-dated values: created_on has 4 rows and last_activity_date has 5 rows beyond today, with ranges extending to 2027-09-03. Future created_on dates will make organization.customer_since look wrong, and future last_activity_date values will suppress the customer rule 2 dormancy override for those accounts.

Customer rule 2 depends on last_activity_date, which is null on 34 rows (3.3%). For those accounts dormancy cannot be evaluated, so the CRM company_status passes through unchanged; flag them for the customer if dormancy classification matters.

primary_contact_email will produce contact rows, but contact.first_name and contact.last_name are required in the target and this file carries no person names (account_owner is the internal Apex owner, not the customer contact). Either a contacts file supplies the names, or the engineer must agree a placeholder/derivation with the customer before contact records can be written.

primary_contact_email has 30 normalized duplicates across 1000 distinct values. The target only requires email uniqueness within an organization, so cross-organization repeats are acceptable; repeats within a single acct_num would collide and are a validation item.

Customer rules 7 through 12 (plan names, quarterly billing, paused/expired status, dead trials, CAD amounts) concern the subscription entity and have no bearing on this file; rule 4 (Strategic accounts always carry an Enterprise subscription) must be applied when the subscriptions dataset is mapped, using the customer_tier decision made here as its input.

Target cross-record rule 'an inactive or churned organization cannot hold a trial or active subscription' interacts with customer rule 6: 'On Hold' accounts are mapped to active here precisely so their paused subscriptions do not violate it, while the 20 'Closed' accounts become churned and any still-active subscription they hold will be rejected at load. Expect reconciliation work on those accounts.

Assumption made: acct_num is used verbatim as organization_id and therefore as the join key for the contact rows derived from primary_contact_email. If the customer intends a different external id scheme, every child-entity mapping changes with it.
contacts.csv: 22 rows (1.0%) have a blank acct_num, so they would produce contacts without the required contact.organization_id; the engineer should decide at validation whether to hold these rows, since cross-record rules require the organization to exist first.

Possible primary-contact conflict: counting the true spellings of is_primary (Y 459, yes 199, TRUE 165, 1 119) gives about 942 contacts flagged primary across only 1,046 distinct account numbers, while Meridian allows at most one primary per organization. Some organizations will have multiple flagged primaries and others none; rule 1 (the account row's primary_contact_email is authoritative where no contact is flagged) should drive the reconciliation, which needs the accounts dataset alongside this one.

Email quality affects the required contact.email field: 106 malformed addresses and, after lower-casing, 66 normalized duplicates across 33 case-variant groups. Meridian enforces email uniqueness within an organization, so duplicates that share an acct_num will collide; this is a validation-stage decision, not a mapping one.

full_name has 88 normalized duplicates and 4 case-variant groups; combined with duplicate emails these likely indicate the same person entered twice. Contact ids are unique, so deduplication will not happen automatically.
last_touch contains 8 future dates (range extends to 2027-08-05) and only 16.6% of values are ISO; any use of this field for the rule 2 dormancy calculation should treat future dates as suspect.

I assumed acct_num in this file uses the same value space as the account number that becomes organization.organization_id; the brief lists no declared reference between the datasets, so this should be verified against the accounts export before loading.
subscriptions.json: sub_id is a clean key: 0 nulls, 0 duplicates, 0 exact duplicate rows across 1003 rows.

acct_num is only 90% unique (903 distinct over 1003 rows), so roughly 100 organizations hold more than one subscription. Load order matters: the cross-record rules require the organization to exist before the subscription references it, and every acct_num must resolve to an organization_id produced from the accounts dataset.

Rule 11 (trials older than 90 days are not migrated) needs a definition of 'trial' before the filter can run: 27 rows carry subscription_level = 'Trial' while 84 rows carry sub_status = 'trialing'. These populations do not line up, so the engineer should confirm which column drives the exclusion and from which reference date the 90 days is counted (export date or go-live date), using the parsed start_dt.

Rule 4 (Strategic accounts always carry Enterprise) is a cross-dataset override that can only be applied after the accounts dataset is mapped; it will silently change plan values that the billing export says are Starter or Professional. Expect a reconciliation list of overridden subscriptions for the customer.

The cross-record rule 'an inactive or churned organization cannot hold a trial or active subscription' will collide with customer rules 2 and 6: dormant accounts become Inactive and Closed accounts become churned, yet this file contains 611 active and 84 trialing subscriptions. Those combinations need a resolution policy (suppress the subscription, or keep the organization active) before load.

seat_count is null in 41 rows (4.1%) but subscription.seats is required; monthly_amount has a minimum of 0 and subscription.mrr_usd is required. Defaults for these blanks and zero-value rows are a validation-stage decision for the engineer.

start_dt contains 2 future dates (range runs to 2027-08-01) and renew_dt contains 80 future dates, which is expected for renewals but not for start dates; the two future start dates should be reviewed at validation.

Per rule 12, 75 CAD rows land in mrr_usd without FX conversion. Since the currency column is not migrated, the USD/CAD provenance is lost in Meridian unless the engineer keeps a separate reconciliation list for finance.
activity.csv: The dataset declares no references, but acct_num is the organization foreign key: all 1000 distinct account numbers must exist as organization.organization_id (loaded first, per the cross-record rules) and must be formatted identically to whatever the organization dataset supplies. Verify this at validation before loading activities.

occurred_at ranges to 2026-09-11, i.e. dates in the future relative to a present-day migration. Flag these for the customer at validation; they also distort business rule 2 (dormant = no activity in the last 18 months), because a future-dated activity would keep an otherwise dormant account looking active.

This dataset is the evidence base for business rule 2: the latest occurred_at per acct_num drives whether an organization should be forced to lifecycle_status = inactive. Plan the activity load (or at least a pre-pass over this file) before finalizing organization.lifecycle_status.

Invoice + INVOICE + Payment = 2563 rows, which is exactly the number of non-null currency values, suggesting amounts are expected only on financial activities. Yet only 1913 amount values parse (3034 null, 650 placeholders), so roughly 650 financial rows arrive without a usable amount. amount_usd is nullable so these will load, but confirm with the customer whether a missing amount on an invoice/payment row is acceptable.
'Invoice' vs 'INVOICE' is a pure case variant of one concept (1 case-variant group reported); no business meaning is lost by folding them, and no customer question is needed for that part.

rows.reason: The catalog states that the customer's legacy account number usually lands in organization.organization_id, and this is the declared key column with 5-digit numeric values that satisfy the target pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$.
Exact name and meaning match with organization.name, which is required; values are company names with no competing target.

Account-level status maps to organization.lifecycle_status (prospect/active/inactive/churned); subscription.status is the wrong home because these values describe the account relationship, not a billing contract, and 6 of 9 values are outside that enum.
The values are a short industry vocabulary that lines up one-to-one with the organization.industry enum; only a code table is missing.

organization.billing_region is the only state/province field in the catalog and the examples ('AB', 'GA', 'Colorado') are exactly state and province values, but the source is labelled headquarters, not billing, so the engineer should confirm the two addresses are the same for Apex.
Country of the account maps to the required organization.billing_country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2); it is the only country field in the catalog.
Exact name and type match with organization.website, which is optional and nullable.

organization.customer_since ('when the relationship started, per the customer's records') is the only organization-level date in the catalog, and the account creation date is the usual proxy for it; no other target fits.

Customer rule 3 says the tier mixes two different concepts: Gold/Silver/Bronze are annual spend bands while Strategic is an executive designation. Meridian's organization.account_priority (standard/priority/strategic) is explicitly 'not the same thing as the plan', so Strategic clearly belongs there, but which spend bands become 'priority' versus 'standard' - or whether the bands should be preserved in organization.tags instead - is a business decision.
Name and meaning match organization.annual_revenue_usd; the values are revenue amounts already denominated in dollars in the examples.
Exact name match with organization.employee_count and the parsed values (22-3999) are plausible headcounts.

There is no email field on organization; customer rule 1 states this column is authoritative for the account's primary contact, so each non-empty value should create (or flag) a contact row with contact.email, contact.organization_id = acct_num and contact.is_primary = true.

These are internal Apex sales-owner person names (993 distinct, 'Firstname Lastname' shapes) and the Meridian catalog has no account-owner or user field on organization; they are not the customer's own contacts, so contact.first_name/last_name would be wrong.

No organization field stores a last-activity timestamp. It could feed activity.occurred_at as a synthetic activity record, but activity.kind is required and this column carries no kind; it is in any case needed as the input to the 18-month dormancy test in customer rule 2, which this mapping already uses for lifecycle_status.

Despite the name this is categorical: only 4 distinct short values across 55% of rows, with shapes like 'aaaaa AA 9999' - it looks like a coded flag rather than free-text commentary. Candidate homes are organization.tags (a label on the account) or activity.description (a note record), and which one is right depends on what the four codes mean.

Unique, fully populated identifier with shape 'CT-000102' that already satisfies the contact.contact_id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$; the deterministic comparison matches on name and the dataset is about contacts.

A 5-digit account number repeating across rows (1046 distinct values over 2279 contacts) is the link from contact to account; the catalog states the customer's legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id, so this is the foreign key contact.organization_id.

The catalog has no single full-name field; contact.first_name and contact.last_name together are the destination, and first_name is the primary landing spot with last_name derived by the same split. Shapes are consistently two tokens ('Aaaaa Aaaaaa').
Email-typed column on the contact row, name matches contact.email, and the target requires an email on every contact.
Phone-typed column on the contact row; contact.phone is the only phone field in the catalog and it requires E.164 (^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$), while no value is currently in E.164 form.

Name and meaning match contact.role, but 9 of 12 values are outside the enum and customer rule 13 covers only 9 of them; 'Ops Manager', 'Purchasing' and 'Main' are uncovered, and rule 13 sends CEO/Owner to primary rather than to the catalog's 'executive' value, which would leave 'executive' unused.
Exact name and meaning match to contact.is_primary; the values are eight spellings of a yes/no flag.

The contact entity has no last-activity or date field at all. The only date-bearing targets are activity.occurred_at (which would require inventing activity records with a 'kind') and organization.customer_since (a different concept), so this field has no safe home without a customer decision; it is also the kind of recency signal rule 2 relies on for dormancy.

There is no marketing-preference or consent field anywhere in the Meridian catalog (contact has only id, organization_id, email, names, phone, role, is_primary), so this flag has nowhere to land. Rule 14 is explicit that opt-out is a marketing preference and that these 214 contacts must still be migrated, so no decision is needed for the contact load itself.
Name and meaning agree: a 100% unique, non-null identifier per subscription row, shape AAA-99999 (e.g. SUB-00415) which satisfies the target pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as-is.

Only 90% unique over 1003 rows (903 distinct), which is the signature of a foreign key to the account, not a subscription key; the target catalog says the customer's legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id, so on the subscription row it is the organization reference.

The values are plan names and the customer's rules 7 and 8 translate them directly into the starter/professional/enterprise enum; the only open point is the 27 'Trial' rows, which name a lifecycle state rather than a plan and have no home in the plan enum.
Name and meaning match the billing_cycle enum (monthly/annual); all six source values are codes or spellings of a billing frequency and rule 9 covers the quarterly case.

These are subscription lifecycle states, so subscription.status is the right home rather than organization.lifecycle_status (which describes the account); rules 10 and the enum cover every observed value.
Direct meaning match to subscription.seats (integer); the export types the same values inconsistently (709 int, 253 str), so only a cast is needed.
Name and meaning match subscription.start_date; the field is a date with only 0.9% nulls, but just 18.7% of values are ISO 8601 so parsing is required.
Name and meaning match subscription.renewal_date; same six mixed date formats as start_dt with 18.2% ISO, 1.6% null.

subscription.mrr_usd is monthly recurring revenue in USD and rule 12 states the billing export amounts are already monthly regardless of billing frequency, so no annualisation or division is needed; the values just need to be parsed out of mixed text ('USD 60', '5100', '$40,000.00').
The subscription entity has no currency field, and rule 12 explicitly says CAD amounts are migrated as-is into USD with a finance true-up afterwards, which makes the column redundant for the load.
Exact name match with activity.activity_id, 100% unique, no nulls or duplicates, and values like 'ACT-0003710' satisfy the target pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as they are.

5-digit account numbers with 1000 distinct values across 4947 rows is the classic legacy account-number foreign key, and the catalog says the legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id; on an activity row it therefore belongs in activity.organization_id (required reference).

Name and meaning match activity.kind, but two of the eight source values ('Ticket', 'Call') have no obvious enum member, and 'Call' has no counterpart at all in [invoice, payment, support_ticket, login, note]; the destination is clear, the value vocabulary is a customer decision.
Exact name match to the required activity.occurred_at datetime; only the four mixed input formats (49.7% already ISO 8601) need normalizing.
Monetary value on an activity row maps to the optional, nullable activity.amount_usd; the name differs only by the _usd suffix and business rule 12 says amounts migrate as USD.

The activity entity has no currency field, the only populated value is 'USD' (2563 rows, the rest blank), and business rule 12 says amounts are migrated as USD as-is, so the column carries no information the target needs.
Exact name match to the optional, nullable activity.description; max length 24 and only 6 distinct templated values fit the string target without change.
